column1: # The variants of the parity harness (ADR-0022), read by
# scripts/check-parity.sh: edits that make a ported rule fire, applied to a copy of every corpus
# tree they are for and compared there as on the tree itself. One row per variant, five or six
# fields separated by tabs: a name of [a-z0-9-], the rule ID it makes fire, the path it edits,
# "sed" with an extended sed expression, "delete" with "-", which deletes a file or a symbolic link
# itself, or "write" with a line, which creates the file the path names and must not find it, and
# optionally the corpus trees it is for, by name and separated by commas; a
# variant without them is for every tree. A variant fails the harness on a tree it is for where
# its edit changes nothing or bash reports no finding of its rule, and when it names a tree the
# docs/adr-index, docs/adr-numbering, docs/adr-header: checks 1, 2, and 7 of check-docs.sh.
# docs/adr-refs, docs/adr-link-targets, docs/adr-supersessions: checks 5, 6, and 8 of check-docs.sh.
# docs/links, docs/section-refs: checks 3 and 4 of check-docs.sh; and the gap in the numbering,
# docs/check-lists, docs/project-layout, docs/skill-pointers: checks 9, 10, and 11 of check-docs.sh.
# docs/inherited-adrs, docs/template-identity: checks 12 and 13 of check-docs.sh.
